text:
alex_support: Customer report — their EU usage bucket shows 0 for the date range 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-15 when they also pick a specific model version. They say billing and raw API logs show requests and tokens counted normally.
acme_ops: Org: acme-inc. Steps: Console > Analytics > Filters: Region = EU, Model = rwd-instruct-4x-quant (version selector) -> Apply -> Chart goes flat. Happens consistently.
alex_support: Thx, can repro on our side with a test org.
maya_analytics: Quick look at the network trace + query logs. UI submits payload with both filters but backend metrics service only receives the model filter. Region seems to be dropped somewhere between frontend serializer and metrics endpoint.
sam_frontend: On it. I see we encode multi-value filters like region as region[]=eu but model.version is sent as a dotted key model.version. Our serializer flattens the filter arrays and then builds the query string; if a dotted key appears it triggers the old "expandNested" path which rewrites the param map and overwrites array entries.
li_dev: That matches a failure mode I saw in the metrics translator. When it sees a key containing a dot it treats the rest as a sub-object and uses object.assign-style merging — if the next filter uses the same top-level key it clobbers previous values. In short: model.version causes the region[] array to be overwritten.
sam_frontend: Example payload from the browser (sanitized):
```
POST /api/metrics/query
{
  "filters": [
    {"key":"model.version","value":"rwd-instruct-4x-quant"},
    {"key":"region[]","value":"eu"}
  ],
  "range": {"start":"2026-03-01","end":"2026-03-15"}
}
```
Network inspector shows server receives: filters=[{"key":"model.version","value":"rwd-instruct-4x-quant"}]
no region entry.
acme_ops: Customer note: they rely on region-level billing reconciliation. This is causing a support escalation.
alex_support: Can we get a quick patch or workaround?
li_dev: Short-term workaround: if you select region first then model second it appears to keep both filters (frontend oddity). Also using the advanced JSON query (raw query editor) bypasses serializer. But we should patch backend serializer.
maya_analytics: I ran the same query against staging after applying a local fix to the serializer — EU bucket returns and numbers match billing exports (+1 tokens).
sam_frontend: I pushed a change to treat dotted keys as atomic strings (no object expansion) and to always append array entries instead of merging. PR linked: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pulls/4823 (will canary).
li_dev: I'm adjusting the metrics translator to be defensive: ignore object expansion on filter keys and validate that filters list length equals payload length before executing. Unit tests added.
sam_frontend: Canary deploy started to 10% of traffic.
maya_analytics: Re-ran repro steps against canary -> EU shows correct counts.
reporting-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0453 and attached timeline.
alex_support: Notifying customer with workaround and ETA for full rollout.
acme_ops: Confirming customer got the message, they will wait for fix. Thanks. :thumbsup:
sam_frontend: Rolling the fix to 100% in 8m.
li_dev: Follow-up: will open a small refactor ticket to unify filter key handling across console + metrics service (link: https://tickets.internal/RED-7821).
alex_support: Marking thread for postmortem notes and add to release notes. Close once 100% done and customer ack.
acme_ops: Customer confirmed after the canary that EU numbers are back. All good here, closing from our side. :tada:
